package_info.package_name: Adwind RAT (delivered via malicious JAR dropper)
package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed as JAR via phishing and GitHub Pages)
package_info.package_versions: Multiple variants (e.g., wucgy3jecwgpv.svg, 6da7uj4b4oi2a.pdf, zpmqwjs.docx, hashes: 8ca09bebe64bc1f8a2b5e50d4883f81d58a9f9fc, 981c98fa370ee934a2754a457a830bcf1e381fbe, ce0b09339b565a6613b505a372f83f4003a81190)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is a heavily obfuscated Java-based dropper that delivers the Adwind RAT, a remote access trojan with extensive info-stealing and surveillance capabilities. It employs multiple evasion techniques, persistence mechanisms, and exfiltrates sensitive data to attacker-controlled C&C servers.

execution_context.file_location: BIFF5-format XLS file (External Reference record) or CSV file (Formula injection)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: cmd /c powershell –executionpolicy bypass –W Hidden –command "[download JAR file zpmqwjs.docx]"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user opening the malicious document, the code executes a hidden PowerShell command to download a JAR file from a remote server, enabling the next stage of malware delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Office documents should not trigger hidden PowerShell downloads of executable content.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Office documents do not execute shell commands or download executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in enterprise environments (rare, and never for JAR downloads).
key_indicators: Download of JAR file disguised as .docx
Use of legacy BIFF5 format and junk characters for evasion

execution_context.trigger: JAR execution (user runs downloaded JAR file)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated Java code using dynamic invocation and decryption function Gv; locale/language/country checks; public IP and geolocation checks via checkip.amazonaws.com and ipinfo.io.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code decrypts and dynamically invokes functions to check system locale, language, and country, then queries external services to determine the public IP and geolocation. If the system is not Turkish, the malware proceeds to execute its payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware evasion via locale and geolocation checks is a common anti-analysis technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Java applications do not perform anti-analysis checks or restrict behavior based on country.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Region-locked software (e.g., DRM), but not for evasion.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code queries installed antivirus products using WMIC and sends the results to the C&C server, enabling attacker reconnaissance.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware commonly enumerates security products to tailor attacks or evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software rarely needs to enumerate antivirus products.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code writes a registry key to ensure the malware is executed on user logon, establishing persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware often uses registry Run keys for persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers may use Run keys, but not for hidden or obfuscated payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-starting legitimate applications (e.g., antivirus, cloud sync).
key_indicators: Registry Run key for obfuscated JAR

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Adwind RAT core: screenshot capture, webcam/microphone access, file theft, keystroke logging, VPN certificate collection, lateral movement, C&C communication (e.g., connect to 21736.xyz:1505).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enables remote access, captures screenshots, records audio/video, steals files and credentials, logs keystrokes, collects VPN certificates, and communicates with the attacker's C&C server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This is the core RAT functionality, enabling full compromise and surveillance.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate Java application should perform all these actions without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote support tools (with explicit user consent and transparency).

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code uses attrib.exe to set the malware file as hidden, reducing visibility to the user.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware often hides its files to evade user detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications rarely hide their executables.
key_indicators: Use of attrib.exe to hide files

attack_chain.action: Phishing email with malicious Office attachment (XLS/CSV) sent to victim.
User opens document, triggering hidden PowerShell command to download obfuscated JAR file.
attack_chain.leads_to: JAR file is downloaded and executed.

attack_chain.action: JAR file executes, performing locale, language, and geolocation checks to evade analysis.
attack_chain.leads_to: If not in Turkey, malware proceeds to next stage.

attack_chain.action: JAR queries installed antivirus products and sends results to C&C.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains reconnaissance on victim's defenses.

attack_chain.action: JAR writes registry key for persistence and hides its files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware persists across reboots and remains hidden.

attack_chain.action: Adwind RAT payload activates, enabling remote access, surveillance, and data theft.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains full control and exfiltrates data to C&C.

behavioral_signatures: Office document triggers hidden PowerShell or shell commands
Download and execution of JAR files disguised as documents
Obfuscated Java code with dynamic invocation and decryption routines
Locale, language, and geolocation checks prior to payload execution
Registry Run key creation for persistence
Use of attrib.exe to hide files
C&C communication to suspicious domains on non-standard ports
RAT behaviors: screenshot, webcam, keystroke logging, credential theft
file_indicators: Office attachments with legacy BIFF5 format and junk characters
Downloaded files with document extensions but JAR content (e.g., .docx, .svg, .pdf)
Hidden files named 'Uninstall' or with attractive icons
network_indicators: Connections to checkip.amazonaws.com and ipinfo.io for geolocation
Outbound connections from Java processes to unknown domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents that execute PowerShell or shell commands, especially those downloading JAR files. Flag downloads of files with document extensions that contain Java bytecode. Detect obfuscated Java code with dynamic invocation and anti-analysis checks. Alert on WMIC queries for antivirus products and suspicious registry Run key creation referencing Java/JAR files. Monitor for outbound connections to known C&C domains and non-standard ports from Java processes. Look for RAT behaviors such as screenshot capture, webcam/microphone access, and keystroke logging.
